utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before I give the opportunity to the Prosecution to call its next witness, I'd first like to respond to a request made earlier by Ms. Loukas. She asked the Chamber for guidance on the use of the Rule 89(F) procedure. That was already quite some time ago. But it has some relevance for the examination of expert witnesses as well, so I'll give the guidance. And it also, as I said, gives some guidance for experts. On the 21st of October, 2004, the Defence, you, Ms. Loukas, asked the Chamber for guidance on the use of the Rule 89(F) procedure. The Defence said that, in that instant, that the Prosecution had inappropriately designated Witness 144 as a Rule 89(F) witness. The Defence compared that choice with the choice made by the Prosecution to examine the next witness, Mr. Pasic, as a non-89(F) witness. The Defence suggested, at least to my understanding, that the Chamber should designate two categories of witnesses: One category constituting those fact witnesses who may be examined using 89(F), and the second constituting those fact witnesses who may not. On the 10th of November, Mr. Stewart has raised a -- although a slightly different issue, namely, that a number of important allegations are to be found in various parts of Mr. Bjelobrk's statement, and that these allegations were not explored in examination-in-chief, that is to say, that they were not elicited orally. In relation to the point raised by Ms. Loukas, the Chamber's view, the issue is not one of categorising witnesses, it is an issue of categorising content. There is no dispute that the efficiency attained by the use of 89(F) procedure must be balanced against the accused's right to a fair trial. The Chamber, and of course the Defence, must be given a fair opportunity to assess the evidence of a witness on important matters during the examination-in-chief. Accordingly, evidence concerning significant acts and conduct of the accused, evidence relating to issues critical and pivotal to the Prosecution's case, and evidence concerning persons or events significantly proximate to the accused should be presented orally by the witness in examination-in-chief. I've called these three criteria. It is true of any witness that if his or her evidence meets one of these three criteria, that portion of the evidence must be elicited orally. Other evidence which does not have these characteristics may be admitted in written form by way of the 89(F) procedure. The test is always content, not the type of witness. I will now address the point raised by Mr. Stewart. It follows from what I just said that if any part of the statement of a witness meets one of the three criteria, and if the witness is not examined on that part of the statement, then that part of the statement must be redacted and it will not be admitted into evidence. I would like to add a related remark about expert witnesses, and that is, as I explained, the reason why I give this guidance at this very moment. There is no doubt that, for an expert opinion to have any value, the facts on which it is based must be before the Court. This does not mean, however, that the present Bench Finds it necessary or even advisable to examine every item of supporting material behind every opinion expressed by an expert. We, that is the Judges, are content to be guided by the parties of the expert which are critical and pivotal to this case and to the corresponding underlying documentation. Unchallenged opinions will be assessed by the Chamber in light of the relevance these opinions appear to have for the case as a whole. The basis for inferences critical for the findings in this case will be duly examined and checked by the Chambers, while unchallenged peripheral opinions will be, as a rule, accepted as such. A practical consequence of the above remark is that the Chamber does not expect the examining party to present to its expert witness each and every item of the often myriad supporting materials underlying his or her report. It suffices to have the expert confront those items which underpin important or contested opinions. The other items may be proffered and, of course, if necessary, also challenged, for admission into evidence after the expert has completed his or her testimony. I turn finally to the 89(F) procedure as adopted at the 65 ter conference on the 16th of April, 2004. In light of our experience with the procedure thus far, and in light of my comments of a moment ago, the Chamber has some modifications to propose, and I'll hand them down on a sheet of paper showing the modified parts in italics. It will be provided to the parties later. It is a refinement of the earlier instructions. So that will be given to the parties later on. Again, the reason why we come back to the 89(F) procedure is because there is some link to the expert witnesses, as I just set out. Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. We are, of course, grateful for the guidance that the Trial Chamber has given in relation to the 89(F) procedure. There's just one point that I'd also like to place on the record, that my query was directed to the type of evidence a witness would give, and Your Honour answer has been in those terms as well. And we are, indeed, grateful for that clarification and delineation, as there seem to be some misunderstanding and misuse up to that point of the 89(F) procedure. And we are, indeed, grateful for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Loukas. Mr. Hannis, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We are, Your Honour. I did want to address, with the Court's procedural matters with regard to how I intend to proceed with marking exhibits for this witness and presenting her exhibits. I can do that while she's in the room or before she comes in --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I say that I have a couple of things, nothing to do with this witness, that I would be grateful raising, but I'm in Your Honours' hands --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time do you need for it, and is there any urgency --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Very short points, Your Honour, not more than five minutes overall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The first is this, your Honour. It's really to follow on from yesterday, which is why I raise it now. In relation to the submissions made by Mr. Tieger, and Your Honours will recall his description of what was done with this CD, what was done with that index, and so on, Your Honour, I did take the trouble to confirm with my case manager the specific example that I had given Your Honours about the CDs and the hard disks. I was both right and wrong. I was wrong in the incidental, trivial way that apparently the Prosecution CDs were not brought to us to put on our hard disk, but our hard disk went to them to put the CDs on. That's a difference of no distinction whatever. Where I was correct in what I informed the Trial Chamber about was that it was the Prosecution's suite of CDs which was put on our hard disk, and it was not simply that they came along. And I won't repeat the language I used yesterday. It wasn't that they came along and did the job for us of putting our own CDs on our own hard disk. But beyond that, Your Honour, without going into painful detail this morning, my case manager came to the conclusion at one point that everybody in court had got it wrong on every single point throughout the entire day. But she did come down a little bit from that proposition in the end. But certainly, from my discussion with her, was that it seemed that Mr. Tieger's account, let's say, is open to serious discussion, Your Honour. So it leads to this conclusion: That if there is any question of the Trial Chamber attaching any weight to the outline that Mr. Tieger gave as to what's happened, then, Your Honour, we would like to have the opportunity of addressing those points specifically before Your Honours reach a decision. On the other hand, if Your Honours are content to disregard what was said, and of course Mr. Tieger is not in court so it's a little bit hard to be suggesting you might disregard everything he said yesterday when he's not here, then the problem's solved. But, Your Honour, that's the position. We -- it was a detailed list of items. It is open to considerable question as to whether it was done in the way described, and there we are, Your Honour, on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether or not to ignore that. Mr. Hannis, you have heard Mr. Stewart, as he did yesterday, has contested at least that part of the statement given by Mr. Tieger yesterday. The Chamber is not seeking lengthy oral argument on that because it seems not to be critical for the decision to be taken, although it might not be totally irrelevant. If there's any reason for Mr. Tieger to come back to it, so that means he considers it's of rather great importance, then we'll hear from you. If we don't hear by today, then we'll just accept the way Mr. Stewart perceived the hard disk travelling and filled with information from CDs that were not in a similar way organised in the previous CDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. I'll check with Mr. Tieger and inform the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- register some discomfort at the distinction between -- the phrase "not critical for the decision" and then "not totally irrelevant." We feel uncomfortable something you regard as not critical but not totally irrelevant. It is an unsatisfactory distinction, with respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I said "not totally irrelevant," because you asked us to ignore it. Then I sought a way out, and I thought it was not of great importance for our decision. And at the same time, I said, since it might not be totally irrelevant, the general observations made, and you attacked it on a specific point; therefore, the Chamber would like to know whether the Prosecution accepts your criticism, yes or no, and we have given an opportunity for Mr. Tieger to come back to it. If he doesn't do that, we accept your criticism.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The other point, Your Honour, does relate, and as sometimes happens, I can certainly go a few sentences at the very least into the matter in open session, but I'm aware, Your Honour, that every time we're discussing something which relates to something which has happened in private session, we have to proceed rather carefully. And it relates to an exchange which took place. I've got it at page 3 of yesterday's transcript. And Your Honours indicated an imminent decision which you propose to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And I had expressed a grievance with the Trial Chamber, or Your Honours' observation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- in saying that there would be certain aspects that there perhaps was no need to draw the attention of the public to. Your Honour, having looked at that transcript, the extent of my acceptance of what made sense - I hope that's not regarded as an offensive way of putting it, Your Honour - but my acceptance of what made sense is really very limited, Your Honour, and the Defence would not, with respect, accept the comments that, without argument, the comments that Your Honour then made immediately after I had said that that made sense, in principle, and I have no further observation. In a nutshell, Your Honour, the position is this: An indication was given by the Trial Chamber, as it was then constituted before Christmas, that it was inclined, I think that was the phrase, the Trial Chamber was inclined to lift the private session protective nature -- protective measures in relation to this particular witness' evidence, and, in effect, invited submissions on the footing that it was quite clear that the invitation was, to anybody -- either party who was going to oppose that. So in circumstances where the Defence had no opposition whatever to a total lifting, we made no submissions pending any submissions being made by the Prosecution. So no submissions were made. Yesterday, the indication that there might be some -- a very substantial lifting but with some reservations just leaves this, Your Honour, that before a final decision is taken in relation to continuation of protection in relation to any material, the Defence would wish to make submissions. So there are two ways of doing it, Your Honour. We'd suggest the most practical course is this: That, if Your Honours proceed in the way that you do have in mind, and you do give your decision as to what lifting of the confidentiality and private session is to occur, but then, seeing what is left, that Your Honours then have in mind to keep private and keep confidential, before a final decision is made in relation to those items, would the Trial Chamber then give the Defence the opportunity of making submissions. And we suggest that's a more practical course because, after all, we will then at that point know where Your Honours at least provisionally are proposing to draw the line between what's lifted and what isn't lifted, so that will make the submissions more productive because they will be directed towards -- when we specifically know what it is we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether an opportunity will be given to make any oral submissions is another matter. But the first to come is a decision to make public the testimony and the exhibits related to that, and then we'll deal with the rest of it. Whether you'll be invited to indicate what, in that case, the Defence would consider should not be made public or what should be made public, or whether we come with a suggestion what the Chamber is inclined to make public or not, and to give an opportunity to the parties to give a comment on that, we'll consider that at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I reserve at this point, without entering into further unrespectful debate, but, Your Honour, an opportunity to a party, having given an occasion -- before Christmas, there would be a complete removal, an opportunity for a party to make observations, make some sort of submissions before a final decision is made is elementary fair procedure, we suggest, Your Honour, so that we hope that when the point comes, the Defence will -- whether it's written, oral, whatever, whatever combination, we hope there will be no decision made against us without the opportunity of making submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it making public certain the testimony and the exhibits is not necessary the end of the story. The confidentiality could be lifted on any private-session debate on the matter prior to the testimony at hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour has it precisely, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll consider that. Anything else? If not, then, Mr. Hannis, it is you who is going to examine the expert Witness, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, yes. It is me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. If I may explain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- how I observe this. Ms. Hanson's expert report we intend to mark as one exhibit, give it one number. Then we have a set of 16 binders that we call the master binders with 468 separate tabs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand they get one number and just a tab number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: One number with the tabs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Ms. Hanson, I take it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're the only one I've said good morning to. I've forgotten to say good morning to all the rest of those in the courtroom. Good morning, Ms. Hanson. Before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. That, of course, for an expert is not all, because, in your expert report, and I take it also in your answers, you'll give expert opinion which requires you, apart from that, of course, everything should be in accordance with the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, but also to give a sincere, to the best of your abilities, the -- your opinion as an expert. I take it you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I invite you to make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Hanson, there seems to be some kind of -- it used to be called a Mexican dog, I think, this noise coming around. Perhaps the technicians could pay attention to that. Please be seated, Ms. Hanson. You will first be examined by Mr. Hannis, counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'd like to continue with a little explanation on the exhibits. I think it will be useful for the witness as well. utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, with regard to the presentation binders, we propose just to hand up the first two binders to Your Honours and the Defence because I don't think we'll get beyond those first 81 items certainly before the first break. Some items appear more than once, but because they appear at different times in our presentation, we put in a second copy of the same item at the appropriate tab so that you don't have to go back and forth in your binders. We can just simply proceed from 1 through 330 in the course of the presentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And lastly, before I begin with my examination of the witness, I would like to explain how we've marked the tabs in the presentation binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll wait for the Defence to have a chance to look at theirs. You'll see the first tab, and on the right it's marked "presentation binder number 1, presentation tab number 1." On the upper left, there's a space for the Prosecution exhibit number, which will be given as we go along. Below that we have the master binder number and the master tab number, which should be, in essence, the exhibit number or the subnumber for the exhibit number. And that tab is appearing on your screen, I think, as well, from Sanction. And then we have information about the ERN of the original, the English translation, and some information about the date and the title of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour. Now I'd like to begin. First of all, Your Honour, we don't have a copy of her report here. I'll have that delivered that later and we want to give that a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to work with the copy of the report I've annotated myself, and this is also an indication that the Chamber has carefully read the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we give that a number? And we'll furnish a hard copy to the Registry at the next break.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The expert report will be Prosecution Exhibit P528.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then, Your Honour, for the master binders with the 468 tabs, we'd like to give that a separate number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The master binders will be Prosecution Exhibit P529.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Examined by Mr. Hannis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, I'd like to start now with asking you, first of all, if we could put up your CV, and I'd like to just summarise briefly your education and employment background. And if I leave something out or say it wrong, will you please advise me?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.text: You graduated from Harvard University in 1984 with a bachelor of arts in Russian and Soviet studies.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we can read the CV, and it might even give us some -- unless there's anything specific you'd like to -- but what you have read now is just a repetition of what we can read.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. I just wanted to do a little bit for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. Ms. Hanson, if we say that there's no need to testify about it, it's not because it's not important, it's just that we get the information just as well by reading it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: Yes. The ERN is consistent with the Trnovo documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab number 6, which is Hanson master binder 1, master tab 28.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: That's number 100.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The information on the tab reflects Sarajevo. And tab number 7, master tab number 32.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is 0 -- 10 or 101-3, and this one was found in Bosanski Petrovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presentation tab number 8?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are now going through all the numbered copies of these instructions, I mean, the instructions, as such, and several numbered versions of it are in evidence. What's, at this moment, the use of saying number so and so, we found there. Is there any dispute about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Defence would actually like to know, Your Honour, what the evidence is. If it's -- if there's a clear -- I don't mind whether the witness confirms it by reference to a list or whether we're told one by one. It's not for the Prosecution's case as to which we suspect it would be, and we would like to know which of these documents is said to come from where, then, Your Honour, one way or another, in the most efficient way, we must hear it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has this not be set out in the footnotes of the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, most of these are in the report. As she mentioned, tab number 3 from Livno was a new one. I have two more to go and then we've going to have some explanation about the significance of these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I apologise for taking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We now just identified these documents as the footnote material, plus one, as far as I understand. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab number 8 in the presentation binder, master tab number 35.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Number 104, and this one is different. It has a line on top indicating that it was sent by fax on the 23rd of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall where that faxed version of 104 was obtained from?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Also from Sarajevo, I believe from the briefcase of Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab number 9, which is master tab number 34.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It's another version of 104. It doesn't have the fax line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, if we can go to tab number 10, which is master tab number 23. Again, I think you've indicated that this translation is the version that you prefer to work from?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is the most complete translation, so that's why I included it there as the -- my screen is blank, but that's what the ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think it will be coming up shortly.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is number 093 which was from the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the -- what was the full title of this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: "The Instructions on the Organisation and Activities of Organs of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina in Extraordinary Circumstances."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many municipalities were there in Bosnia before the war?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Approximately 110.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the highest number you saw in any of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the highest number of the copies found in our collection?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to show you tab 11 in the presentation binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone please, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you tab 11 in the presentation binder, which is from master tab 51. Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It is minutes of the meeting of the secretariat of the SDS of Bosanski Petrovac on the 26th of September, 1991. Under item 2, it says that "the instructions for the organisation and activities of organs of the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina in extraordinary circumstances should be retyped in seven examples," and each member of the secretariat should get a copy. If you'll recall, the copy from Bosanski Petrovac had a different numbering than all the others. It was 101-3. That would be consistent with the idea that it was retyped in multiple copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, in connection with that, I would like to remind the Court of the testimony from Mr. Hidic from Bosanski Petrovac who talked about finding copies of documents in the municipality building when he returned in 1995, and some of his testimony about various copies in various typefaces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in your report, you indicate that these documents were issued by the SDS Main Board or the SDS Crisis Staff. What was the basis for your assertion to that effect in the report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: On the front page of the document, it says it's coming from the SDS Main Board. The last page is type-signed "SDS Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did your examination of the material show with regard to how this report was distributed, and to whom it was distributed?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: The diary of Karadzic chef de cabinet, Grkovic, indicates that on the 20th of December there was a meeting of the Main Board in the deputy's club.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we'd like to show you presentation tab number 12, which is master tab number 374.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've been putting the B/C/S copy up on the screen because Ms. Hanson reads B/C/S, but I don't know if the Court would prefer to see the English. We can proceed either way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have the English in front of us, and if Ms. Hanson works on the B/C/S original, perhaps it's better to have the B/C/S original on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We'll continue in that fashion, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, did I interrupt your explanation of this one?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: I'm just going to say that that is the page that I referred -- that I found the reference from the Grkovic diary, that at 4.00 on the 20th of December there was a meeting of the Main Board in the deputy's club.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I feel a bit guilty, saying both to the interpreters and to you, Mr. Hannis, because I'm trying to speed up. But not necessarily in the speed of speaking. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll try to slow down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next I would like to show presentation tab number 13, which is master tab number 36. This is an excerpt from the minutes of the Bratunac SDS. Can you explain what you've got on the screen in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is further indication of the receipt and distribution of the 19 December instructions. At a meeting of the SDS Municipal Board on the 23rd of December, the president of the Municipal Board, Miroslav Deronjic, told the Municipal Board about a meeting of what he calls the presidency of the SDS in Sarajevo, and he distributes material from this presidency session. I would like to point out that no where else in documents about the SDS do we see reference to a body called the presidency of the SDS. I take this to mean a meeting of the leadership of the SDS, because we don't see a presidency as such anywhere else. The minutes indicate that he read from this material of the SDS leadership, and they then acted on it. He says that two variants are foreseen, A and B. "For us, variant B, second degree of organisation applies." If you'll recall, variant B, in the A and B document, meant Serbian minority municipalities. Bratunac was a Serbian minority municipality. Then the other steps taken, holding an assembly, forming a Crisis Staff, and introducing duty watches, those are all parts -- elements of the A and B document. So to my mind, these minutes indicate that he received the A and B document at a meeting of the SDS leadership in Sarajevo sometime before the evening of the 23rd of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if Mr. Deronjic was a member of the Main Board?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: I do not believe -- not at this time. He became a member of the Main Board, I think, in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've described the difference between the variant A and variant B municipalities, with A being Serb-majority and B being Serb-minority municipalities?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there another dichotomy in --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, there was also the first and second degrees of organisation. Basically, variant A served majority municipalities. First degree was preparations, and second degree was activation. A similar dichotomy under variant B, Serb minority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the instructions indicate with regard to forming Crisis Staffs who should be the members of Crisis Staffs in the municipalities?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's spelled out for both variant A and variant B. Is it possible to look at that document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It was -- two tabs back was the preferred translation -- was the preferred copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll put that up for you in just a second.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's presentation tab 10 that we've got back on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And if, at -- I'd like you to pay some additional attention to tab 12 as well, because we got a bit stuck there through the speed-of-speech issue, and I'm a bit confused about it. So if, after tab 10, you would also pay more attention to tab 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, would it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would it be easier to go back to 12?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I've got a specific question. Ms. Hanson, you started saying that -- it says something about a meeting with, you said "indicates that on the 23rd of December, there was a meeting of the Main Board in the deputy's club."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, the 20th of December. I may have misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly what my problem was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Grkovic diary shows that there was a meeting on the 20th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It shows the 23rd in the transcript. No, I don't know who made the mistake. That at least clarifies the issue. And then I also do understand that it's not highlighting in the English translation, but it's just a graphical -- so it's the first item at 4.00 on the 20th which is of importance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, then, I think you wanted to have a look at a copy of the variant A and B instructions?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. You had asked me about who goes in -- the composition of the Crisis Staff. For reference, I thought it would be easier, but I can tell you in general terms, that the variant A and B document specifies that in both municipalities -- both variant A and variant B municipalities, the leadership of the municipal party is to go into the Crisis Staff. If I could see, perhaps, the second -- the next page of the document. I don't know if it's possible. The president of the municipal board, the president of the municipality in the majority municipalities, the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I interrupt you for a second.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the Sanction presentation, I think we now have a page up that may assist.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: The next page would be even better. I have a copy, or could you provide me with a copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a hard copy of number 93.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we may hand this to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This would be the B/C/S version from tab 10.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It's on page 3. It specifies: "All members of the secretariat of the party," which means the president, vice-president, and secretary of the municipal board, those people who have a function in the municipal government, or alternatively, the SDS candidates for those positions, that is, the president of the municipal assembly or the president of the executive board, the head of the police station or the commander of the police, the commander or the head of the municipal board -- staff of the Territorial Defence, the secretariat of the -- municipal secretariat for national defence or other people who have municipal functions in a municipality. Also, deputies to the Bosnian Serb assembly, and members of the Main Board of the SDS are all supposed to go into the Crisis Staff, which means it's the leadership at the municipal level, it's people in the municipal government and people with ties to the republican level of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with that, I know in your report, I think in paragraph 16, you indicated that, in effect, these measures made the Crisis Staffs shadow governments, armed with a concrete plan for action. Can you give us some example of that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. A member of the Prijedor Crisis Staff explicitly referred to the Crisis Staff as a shadow government --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can halt you there for a minute and we'll put up the next tab.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is presentation tab 14, master tab number 38, and it's a transcript of a radio broadcast from Prijedor in April of 1995, on the third anniversary of the takeover.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: The highlighted section simply says --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the English, that would be page 7, about two-thirds of the way down the page. I don't know if it's highlighted in your copy or not. Mr. Kovacevic is speaking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's right after the number 25.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it. It's the middle of page 7. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It says, "we had earlier formed the so-called shadow government." And this whole broadcast is devoted to the takeover of Prijedor and the actions of the Crisis Staff at the time. I just found that a significant phrase, because the A and B document specifies that people who are in the municipal government go in the Crisis Staff, and he calls it a shadow government. We have also other references to the A and B document as a plan for real functions taking over power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who Mr. Kovacevic was in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: I do not recall his exact position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me go next to tab 15 in the presentation binder, which is master tab number 376.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an intercepted telephone conversation and we'd like to play a segment. And I believe in English, the portion we're going to be listening to is found at page 7 of the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You remember the procedure, that it will be translated so we are not just listening to it, but it will be translated so that it also appears on the French transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see the yellow bar moving through the transcript, but I don't hear any sound at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have the same experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Until we can deal with that technical difficulty, we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's ask someone. Is there a specific portion to be played of this relatively lengthy intercept, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: There is, Your Honour. It's a very short segment. I could hand Ms. Hanson a copy of the B/C/S transcript and ask her to read that and have it interpreted, if we can proceed in that fashion for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, if it properly reflects the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the ERN --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections by the Defence if Ms. Hanson would read the B/C/S portion?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not by the Defence, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, she'll be reading from page number ERN 03244714, and in the English, that's at page 7, near the bottom, where Mr. Karadzic begins with "second of all."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Starting with the speech of Radovan Karadzic. [Interpretation] Second of all, we have to take into account that -- [In English] I'm getting the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's our practice that if we read, we usually speak -- all our ears are hurt. It's the same for everyone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I find it difficult to read the B/C/S while hearing the English. I wasn't expecting it, but I will concentrate now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one forces you to listen to the English. If you switch to the B/C/S, you will hear your own voice, and then it will be translated. We have the English text in front of us and we can read it all. If you start reading, it is our experience that text that is read is usually spoken more quickly than text we have to invent while speaking, so will you please read it slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] With the election of a new one, we must take into account the fact that we need a person who is not a person from some institutes or university. Miroslav: Yes, because this is not the time for arts and sciences. Karadzic: Now, it is not a time for sciences. It's time to have people take over realistic functions, and there is nothing -- when we're talking about the paper, I don't know, this document of ours, degree 1, degree 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the speakers in that conversation when you listened to it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: I recognised the voice of Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the document, the other speaker was identified as Miroslav, no further name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What led you to believe that they were talking about the variant A and B instructions?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: The reference to "level 1, level 2," and "a paper of ours," he says, "level 1, level 2," with a list of real functions for the takeover of power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this conversation was dated on the 7th of January, 1992; is that consistent with the timing of when this was happening?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it is consistent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next I would like to go to presentation tab 16, this is another intercepted conversation, master tab 377.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document title refers to it as an intercepted conversation between Tintor and Mr. Krajisnik. However, the entire document is actually notes of more than one conversation, and the conversation that Ms. Hanson has referred to in this document is actually between two other speakers. It's the second conversation, beginning near the bottom of the first page in your English copy, where the speakers are identified as Rajko Kopravica and General Djurdjevac. This is a conversation we do not have an audio for. The transcript is prepared from the handwritten notes of operatives that were taking this conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, can you tell us about this conversation?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: In this conversation, Rajko Kopravica, the president of the SDS Vogosca, is calling General Djurdjevac, the commander of the 4th Corps Sarajevo. He is concerned that some Muslim forces are coming towards his area, and the General tells him: "Act according to the instructions for the work in crisis situations. You know those instructions."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this conversation was referred to as occurring on the 3rd of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tab number 17, I believe you indicated, was for purposes of identifying who Djurdjevac was.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Right. It's simply a reference for the Court to see who Djurdjevac was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So presentation tab number 17, Your Honour, which is Hanson master tab 457, was put in to show who Vojislav Djurdjevac was. In the interests of saving time, I would propose to move on to tab 18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with regard to implementing these December 19th instructions, did you find that, indeed, they were acted upon in various municipalities in Bosnia at the time?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. I saw many references to these documents -- to indicate these documents were received and implemented in late December, and some of them have explicit references to the instructions; others are simply references consistent with the content of the instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me go through some of these with you quickly. Tab number 18, which is master tab number 40, could you tell us where that's from?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It's the conclusions of the municipal board of the SDS Zvornik from the 22nd of December. They introduce -- here are introducing duty watches, which, as we know, is consistent with the instructions, and a Crisis Staff is formed with a command -- commandant, a commander, as also noted in the instructions. A coordinator for negotiations with the SDA, that's also specified in the instructions. This is a -- "Crisis Staff formed late December" is consistent with the A and B instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab number 19, master tab number 41.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: These are minutes from the executive board of the municipal board of SDS Kljuc, from the 23rd of December, 1991. The first item of the agenda is -- reading -- "familiarising with the decisions of the Serbian assembly and the material which has arrived." Under agenda item 1 in the minutes, it says: "Veljko Kondic familiarised those with the instructions in organising and actions of the Serbian people of BiH. All organs are obliged to act in accordance with these instructions." Further down, another member says he can't accept anything that Karadzic says without looking at it. I intend to look at this in more detail when we look at a Kljuc case study. But if you could just go to the next page of that -- no, it's not -- I intend to look at the Kljuc documents in more detail when we do a case study of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I don't oppose that. It is Mr. Hannis who is examining that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next tab would be tab 20, master tab 378.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is a meeting of the Crisis Staff of the SDS Novo Sarajevo on the 23rd of December, 1991. It says that they examined the material received from the Main Board of the SDS. First degree, under item 1 -- well, they specify various items. Item 2, they form a secretariat. You will recall that item 2 in the variant A level, first degree, refers to a secretariat. Item 3 similarly refers to forming a Crisis Staff and nominating a coordinator for relations with the HDZ and SDA. That is also consistent with item 3 of the variant A and B. So it's -- while it doesn't specify the name of the instructions, it's a reference consistent with the A and B variant document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The item numbers here list -- line up number-wise with those items in the instructions themselves?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. For example, under item 9, they specify civil defence, MUP, and Territorial Defence. Item 9 under variant A level 1 also refers to those. So it's consistent throughout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the end of the first paragraph, is there a reference to which degree or which stage this referred to?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it says first degree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what -- which type of municipality was Novo Sarajevo at that time? Was it Serb majority or minority, A or B?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: I believe it was -- actually, I can't remember. I don't recall. I have the census here, but I don't know if -- off the top of my head, I would have said it was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's all right, if you don't recall. Let me go on to the next tab.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just ask one question in relation to that. In the document, we see the word "reserve" appear just a couple of lines from the bottom, but it's in quotation marks. Could you explain what it means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think a reasonable interpretation would be a reference to arms, because it says, equipment, "oprema", which is used for general military equipment, and the "means" being in quotation marks, I take it to mean not simply money, because it also talks about financial, "sredstva", money means --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Reserves is to be understood in financial terms? Because the translation says "reserves."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think "sredstva" I would more usually translate as simply means. It doesn't necessarily mean financial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have difficulty understanding the line, because then it reads in the translation, "special powers to purchase equipment and means." Would that mean that we would buy means or that we would get money or things or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Things which are means to an end. Perhaps, I don't know if the interpreters can offer a better translation of "sredstva", but it means concrete things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It can mean concrete things as well as financial means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's still a bit misty. But perhaps if you could read the line slowly to see whether the interpreters can help us out, because they have not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Read it in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Special authority for the purchase of equipment and means, Dragan Mucetic will be in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So whatever that means will be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- doesn't refer to money. Two sentences down, if I could just read that sentence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obtain financial means for the needs of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then still the translation to "reserves" in the first time that sredstva is not entirely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears in between as well, it seems. I have no idea about the B/C/S, but it appears that the same word appears not just two sentences down but in between. I don't know whether that gives any clue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would maybe refer to communication equipment. I'll read that sentence too. I don't know the translation, what you have there, but I would translate it there as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, this is not the core of this document, but we always prefer to understand the documents whenever we see it. Please proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll move on to tab 21, then, which is master tab 42. This is a document from the 24th of December, 1991. Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It's minutes from the executive board of the Serbian municipal assembly of Bosanska Krupa, on the 24th of December, 1991. Under agenda item 3, item A is another reference to the instructions on the formation of Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, is there any reason why there's no English translation of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I didn't ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have an English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tab 21. Then I'm the only unfortunate one who has to do without. I'll overcome that. It's good for my B/C/S training anyhow. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, you passed the test. We know you're following along now. We will furnish you a copy during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned item number 3, implementing the instructions of establishing a Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know if we have in Sanction a copy of the next page where there's a further elaboration of that agenda item.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It looks like we don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But in the hard copy, Your Honours, you'll see at the bottom of the page there's some discussion of that instruction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with regard to the document, it makes reference to Miroslav Vjestica. Do you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: He was a member of the -- a deputy to the Bosnian Serb assembly from Krupa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand we'll hear more about him later on.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll look at some of his assembly speeches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next, if we can go to tab 22, which is the master tab number 43, a document dated the 24th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: These are notes from a meeting of the Crisis Staff of the SDS for the city of Sarajevo. You'll note, after the list of those present, there's a very clear reference to the A and B document. It says "special assignments according to the instructions on the organisation and activities of organs of the Serbian people in BiH in special circumstances, according to variant B." And I can't actually -- it's not clear -- it says "degree," but I can't see in the original whether it says first or second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: But it's a reference to variant B, a level, and it's a clear reference to the instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next, if we could move to tab 23, that's master tab number 379, a document dated the 25th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is a meeting, an extraordinary session, of the municipal board of the SDS Trnovo, on the 25th of December. And here, agenda item 1 is "instruction on the organisation of the Serbian people in crisis situations." And among the steps taken is forming the Crisis Staff on the basis of the instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The English translation I have refers to setting up -- to set up a Crisis Staff pursuant to the directives. Could you read us the B/C/S word? I know I've heard that translation two different ways.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It is "uputstvo".

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would propose to submit a revised translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, we notice that we have, throughout, we've got -- we're getting, not surprisingly, we're getting a completely different translation -- not completely different, I withdraw"completely." We're getting, of course, a different translation on the transcript as Ms. Hanson reads from B/C/S documents from what we're seeing on the English documents. This is run through the entire morning. I don't know why, in particular, this item gives rise to a need for a revised translation. Directives, instructions, it -- we'd suggest it all pretty much comes to the same fairly clear thing as a matter of language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So try to cut down the unnecessary bits of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm fine to leave it that way. It's only because the variant A and B document is entitled "instructions" specifically that I propose to do that. But I don't think it's necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But I would comment that the very title of the A and B instructions came across differently when Ms. Hanson herself was translating from the B/C/S version, from the conventional label that we've had throughout. We don't quarrel with that, we just note it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I noticed that as well, and of course sometimes, if words have to be translated quickly, and if there are several options, several choices, then it might not always be entirely consistent. The Chamber understands that, the Chamber knows that, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- as it stands now, since the parties have no problems with its directives or instructions, it's close to each other so therefore there's no need to provide a new translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll move to tab number 34, which is master tab 37, a document dated the 27th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: These are minutes from the meeting of the municipal board of SDS Prijedor, on the 27th of December. Under item 1, the president read the instructions which the municipal board of the SDS Prijedor had received from the assembly of the Bosnian people. Because there are two variants, only variant 2 was read out, which relates to the municipality of Prijedor. He read out both variant A and B. Then under -- further down, they form a Crisis Staff, introduce duty watches, and the members of the Crisis Staff are also consistent with the A and B instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the document refers to Simo Miskovic as the president of the Prijedor municipal board. Do you know if he was a member of the Main Board of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think next we're going to move to some intercepts, and because I want to check and see if we can take care of the sound problem, this would be a good time to take a break, if that would be okay with the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis, I think it's approximately time for a break. Nevertheless, I would have one question -- let me just try to... In understanding the reading out, during this meeting on the 27th of December, 1991, it says, "since there were two versions, only version 2, which is relevant for Prijedor municipality, was read out," and then it later says, "having read out all the items in sections A and B of version two." Did I understand that the distinction between the variety A and variety B was whether there was a majority -- a Serb majority or not? So what exactly, then, is version 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think, perhaps, a reasonable explanation would be that a person taken -- it's confused, because there's A, A1, A2, and then B, B1, B2. If they put B for 2 and 1 and 2 for A and B, perhaps he meant through variant B, and then numbers 1 and 2. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It certainly makes sense if they've -- if they had written it down differently, if it said only A and B was relevant for Prijedor and therefore we would add 1 and 2 from the relevant -- but that's not what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's not what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now what it says is totally illogical?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Variant 2, and items A and B, it's not logical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But the other items are consistent with the instructions, the other things they do, Crisis Staff, duty watches, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Ms. Hanson, Prijedor was?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: A Serb minority municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which would have been?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: A variant B. So it would have been a second section of those instructions, but it's B first and then the numbers under it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at least I understand my own confusion. We'll adjourn until five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I neglected this morning to welcome you back and say, Happy New Year to the returning Judges, and welcome to our new Judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, I would like to now go to presentation tab 25, and I think, may be after the next break or certainly by tomorrow, I think we'll make an extra set of the presentation binders for you that will make the process go faster.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: That would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that we have an extra one here that we could give you. We'll give you binder number 1, and presentation tab 25, which is master tab 380. This is an intercepted conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I think we've solved the audio problem, I hope. And for your information, this is a conversation between Radovan Karadzic and a person named Bijelica from Sokolac. On the 27th of December 1991, the segment we're going to play, Your Honours, in the English, is at page 2. About two-thirds of the way down Mr. Karadzic is speaking, and he talks about having many other commitments. And if you're ready, Your Honours, we'll start playing that segment. It's a very short segment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you solved the audio problems. It seems to be not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I heard some audio somewhere, Your Honour, but not in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it the technician hears it quite well, because it seems to come from the technical booth. Is there any way to get that sound to our earphones as well? And then the second question is, Mr. Hannis, you said we'd start on page 2. Could you indicate? I have some difficulties to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The tenth box up from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The tenth box up from the bottom, Radovan Karadzic is speaking. It starts out: "I am not sure ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think we'll try again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] And I have many other commitments. That is why I am not sure about it. We are doing this work. Everything is normal. Excellent. I hear that the municipality is functioning well now. Is this Pajic person good? We're working good. Special assignments, we do it as well. Is the Pajic good? Good indeed. Don't, Marko, treat him well, because it's not, it's a normal thing in a democracy."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, can you tell us what that conversation is about?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Bijelica was the president of SDS municipal board for Sokolac and Pajic was the president of the municipality assembly. I found this passage significant because Bijelica is saying that the municipality is working well, including the special assignments, we are doing the special assignments as well. It's not an explicit reference. At the least, it is certainly indicative of Karadzic being aware of what was going on in the municipalities at this time. But I found the reference to special assignments to be significant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't intend to put tab 26 up on the board. It's a list of personnel, and it was for purposes of identifying Mr. Bijelica's position. In the English document, what's numbered page 10, item number 85, two boxes up from the bottom is where Mr. Bijelica is referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And tab 27 was also for purposes of identification as to his role in the Serb Autonomous Region assembly for the region of Romanija, and on page 2 of 4 at the bottom, he's listed as a speaker at that session. That was the purpose for tab 27.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that information. This is presentation only, so you're not presenting it because it's not footnote material.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you're just telling us that you had in mind at that moment to present this in order to clarify his position, which you finally do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It was just to explain who that person was in relation to the conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You could have done that, yes. Then I have one question, Mr. Hannis. We have some difficulties in following the audio again in tab 25, and I could read more on paper than I heard translated. But we did not have the scrolling text in front of us. So I do understand that you specifically want to draw the attention to the special assignments, and that was still translated, because later on, a few lines were left out in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It seemed to me that -- I'm not sure, but the next to the last box, which was in the hard copy of the transcript was not spoken by the interpreter, and I think it was a matter of trying to catch up with the audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next, I would like to go to presentation tab 28, which is master tab 318. This is another intercepted conversation. This is dated approximately the 1st of January, 1992. And in the English, Your Honour, it begins seven boxes down where Mr. Karadzic is saying, "it's you, professor, right?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're skipping the new year's wishes, which you've already delivered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We'll try to play that for you now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "It's you, professor, right? Yes, it's me, it's me. You know, I didn't want to intorduce myself. I was at this meeting of the municipal staff. I wanted to say something in relation to that. As to the party tomorrow, I would come to say a few things. Radovan KARADZIC: And which municipal staff is that? Micevic: Centre municipality. Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh. That's their legal or ... Micevic: Yes, yes, our crisis. Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh. Good. Micevic: So I've said, I've just arrived from that meeting. The people are running around in circles and they need help, and I don't think I could do that without you. Radovan KARADZIC: Good. Tomorrow I'm going to this Belgrade convention. Micevic: All right. Radovan KARADZIC: I'll be back the day after tomorrow so we'll do it then. Micevic: Right. Okay, I agree. Or should I look for Rajko? Radovan KARADZIC: All right. That wouldn't be bad. Micevic: If Rajko is in Sarajevo, if he can help. Radovan KARADZIC: Yes. Have them give you at the seat, have them find Rajko for you. If Rajko can. Is it urgent? Micevic: It's not that urgent, but they received the documents to act upon. However, there are things that they are incapable of doing. Radovan KARADZIC: Yes. Yes. Micevic: We should help them now so they know what to do with the people and so. Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh. All right. Micevic: That's why I'll look for Rajko tomorrow. Radovan KARADZIC: Mm-hm. Micevic: To the seat and get them to put me in touch with Rajko if he's in Sarajevo. Radovan KARADZIC: All right. All right. Micevic: Fine. By the way, I want you to have a good time in Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, can you tell us about that conversation and how --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the French translation had not finished yet on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we, to the extent possible, could we have the French translation ... Yes, then we can proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I've put the French channel on now and I'll try to make sure that they've finished before I go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, can you explain to the Judges what you believe that conversation has to do with the instructions?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Well, I believe it has to do with the instructions because Micevic is reporting to Karadzic that he was at a meeting of the Crisis Staff of Sarajevo center municipality, and that the people there have received a document. They want to implement it but they need some instructions from the party center. The Rajko he refers to, I believe, is Rajko Dukic, head of the SDS executive board, another leader in the SDS. He's saying they've got the documents, but they need help. And it says "our crisis," meaning "our Crisis Staff" had been meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presentation tab 29, master tab 456, is a document you put in regarding the identification of who Mr. Micevic was.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, simply to show for the Court that Micevic had a position in the Bosnian government, deputy director of education -- a university education fund. He was also an early member of the SDS Main Board, as the next tab indicates. After the intercepts, I simply -- for reference of the Court, I added some documents to show people's identities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with regard to tab 29, Mr. Micevic's name appears under item 14 on the second page. And presentation tab 30, master tab 455, his name is number 24 on that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, in the translation we have number 14 three times, and the number 15, whereas in the original it seems that we go from 14 to 17 in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I'm not following. Are you referring to which tab?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say Micevic is under number 14, but then I have, again, a Mr. Korejica under number 14 and Mr. Subotic as well, three times under number 14 in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The numbering is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The numbering is wrong in the English. He appears to be under the first number 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's so clear that we change in the -- we'll make it 15, 16, 17 -- oh, yes. Yes, Judge Hanoteau draws my attention to the fact that we have three --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: A lot of nines as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: And number 1 as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and number 1 as well, as he said, without his microphone on. Could you please have a look at it and see whether it's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we can provide --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not spend time on it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next I want to go to tab number 31 in the presentation binder, it's master tab 382. This is another intercepted conversation, Your Honours, dated the 6th of January, 1992, between -- purportedly between Radovan Karadzic and a Miroslav Stanic. The portion we want to play for Your Honours in the hard copy, English, on page 2, near the middle of the page, where Mr. Karadzic is saying: "Uh-huh." It's right after Mr. Stanic makes reference to the journalist from Der Spiegel is where we will begin. Another very short segment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh. Stanic: We have formed a Serb municipality and you have that information. Radovan KARADZIC: All right. Stanic: If this thing should go differently, on the 15th, we will have a public promotion that -- Radovan KARADZIC: Yes, yes, and take complete control over your affairs. Stanic: Yes, yes. Everything as it is in the instructions."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, can you tell us about that conversation? Who are the speakers, and how does it relate to the instructions?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Miroslav Stanic was president of the SDS board of Foca and president of the Crisis Staff of Foca. I noted that here there's another reference to "instructions," that the -- that Stanic has instructions which will enable him to take "complete control of your affairs." Also significant, Stanic says to Karadzic "we have formed a Serb municipality as you know". So it's also indicative of general information reporting to Karadzic. He expects that Karadzic knows what they have done in the municipality, including forming a Serb municipality which, as you know, is part of the 19 December instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regarding the identification of the other speaker with Mr. Karadzic, tab 32, master tab 452, can you tell us what that's in there for, and who --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Just simply to show that Stanic was president of the SDS Board for Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, on the English, his name appears on page 4 of 4, the fourth name down in tab 32.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tab 33 was also for identification purposes?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, to show that he was on the Crisis Staff of the Serb municipality of Foca. It does not here list him as president, but he is listed as number 1, first member.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, if I may just interrupt. I think the audio is not going as it should. If I look at the transcript at this moment, we see that not the same text appears as we have in the translation. Sometimes portions fall away. From what I remember is that the text would be provided to the interpreters, that we would take time for the interpreters to read the text because they can't just reproduce on the basis of their hearing.
