It would then take time so that we would have both a correct English transcript and that we'd have time to have it translated into French as well, and that there would always be a possibility for either of the parties to say that what was read is not exactly what was said in the original. This does not go well at this moment. I think it has no great consequences. I haven't heard any complaints, but I'd very much urge you to do it as we agreed and to take care that the transcript properly reflects both in English and in French the content of the intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the moment, it's a rather temporary offer that would possibly save time. Nobody need worry about the Defence's ability to suggest that the text is not being faithfully reduced in the English because right now we have no such facility in court to make any such observation. So that, I hope, will be a very temporary position. But no one need worry about that because we can't do anything about it right anyhow anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we have is Mr. Krajisnik --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but Mr. Krajisnik does not know whether the English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but that's the first step.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, as far as Mr. Krajisnik is concerned, it's important that he hears it in his own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He can check whether the words written in B/C/S are the words spoken in B/C/S, and then you have the disadvantage at this moment that you can't check the translation right away. I do agree with that. It should then be done out of court to the extent --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, it can't be done out of court, with respect, Your Honour. We simply do not have the facilities or the time to do that. We don't have the human resources to do that, Your Honour. Many, many times I have indicated that -- but not as strongly as I am doing now, Your Honour, that simply to brush stuff -- I don't mean that Your Honour is not making a perfectly practical suggestion. But that I'm simply informing the Trial Chamber that what is sometimes a perfectly practical suggestion that these matters get dealt with out of court is impossible. We are absolutely beyond the limit of anything we can cope with out of court, let alone in court. It cannot be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do I understand your point, Mr. Stewart. Since it was of some concern to the Chamber as well, I at least tried to get information on the issue of whether any additional translation facilities would be granted to the Defence if Ms. Cmeric would leave. I was informed, but if it's not correct, please tell me, that at least additional interpretation services were offered to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, the whole question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we are not going again through the total of the facilities. I just wanted to verify --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I wasn't going to, with respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I wasn't going to, Your Honour. I was just making a different observation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I sought first of all a verification of the information that reached me, information that said that at least some additional translation resources were given to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I started off simply saying the whole question, I just wanted to say a sentence. The whole question of resources and money, and I'm not going into it, Your Honour, I'm just saying it is a very big question, many, many different strands to it, and an enormous amount of time has had to be spent on that as well, to the detriment of actually running Mr. Krajisnik's defence in any direct sense. Your Honour, there are -- it is certainly correct that some limited, and everything is limited, some limited interpretation facilities and resources are being made available right now, without us having to get into a big debate about those resources. But they are, in any case, extremely limited, Your Honour, in relation to the task which we would face in achieving anything remotely comparable to the facilities which are offered to us by having a full-time case manager. That's not the fault of the people offering those particular additional resources, which we certainly appreciate as far as they go. But it is a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is $1.000 a month?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It is precisely $1.000 a month, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stewart. Please proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question for the witness. Maybe I wasn't listening carefully, but I did not understand what is the origin of the document under number -- under tab 32? What is the list of the main members of the SDS? We can see Momcilo Krajisnik, and then there are three pages with names. And I did not understand, where does that document come from? Would you please indicate it to us. Do you see which document I'm talking about? It's the last document we've looked at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The list of SDS people? It is from -- it's from the Sarajevo collection, which was taken, from my understanding, from the SDS headquarters in Sarajevo, and it's called "A List of Members of the Main Board of the SDS." I would have to consult the evidence record form to give you more details about where it was found, but it is from the Sarajevo collection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. My case manager has advised me that we provided English transcripts of the remaining intercepts we anticipate playing today, so hopefully that will assist in the process that we've tried to use in the past.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that regard, I would like to go to tab number 34, which is an intercept. This is master tab number 383, a conversation on the 21st of December, 1991, between Radovan Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the portion that we intend to play, in the English, is -- begins at the top of page 3, with "M" for Momcilo Krajisnik being the first speaker, saying "But what do you ..." It's also on the top of page 3 in the B/C/S, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "M: But what do you ... Here, you know what, they told me that the people from Krajina are dissatisfied with that Cizmovic. I don't know, that... R: All right. That's until the New Year, the Serbian New Year, then we'll see. M: But I don't understand, this ... how did the idea come up that we should coordinate this? R: You know what, who will implement what we issued last night? M: This council of ministers. R: But they can't run ... from municipality to municipality. M: Huh? R: They cannot run from municipality to municipality and say do this, do that or that."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We note that we do not have the original transcripts in the B/C/S and therefore cannot verify that the transcript actually reflects the audio.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, my misunderstanding. I guess we furnished the English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think that what we did is -- what we intended to do is that one of the team would listen and see whether what is said reflects what's given in the translation, and that the other interpreter would read it, and since reading out takes more time than following with the eyes, that the team together, the one could confirm that the text, as it appears on paper and more slowly read out by the colleague, would be the text originally spoken in B/C/S. That's what my understanding was of our procedure. Is that sufficient for the interpreters? I'm now listening to the English channel, so if there's any response.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we are reminded now on the procedure we agreed upon at an earlier stage. Please proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will bring down the B/C/S for the booth as well. Your recitation refreshes my recollection about what our practice was as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, can you tell us what your understanding of that conversation is?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik and Karadzic are discussing how to implement something that they issued last night. I note that this conversation took place on the 21st of December, 1991. You'll recall that we know there was a meeting of the Main Board in the deputy's club on the 20th, and that the 19 December instructions were distributed at about this time. In order to implement the thing they issued on the 20th of December, Karadzic says they need a coordinator to run from municipality to municipality, say, Do this, do this, do this. The coordinator they've appointed is Cizmovic, so we'll look at more about Cizmovic. And I think when we see all the series of documents, it will make -- the significance will emerge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. With that, then, let's move to tab number 35, which is master tab number 384, and it's a document dated the 21st of December, 1991. Can you tell the Judges what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It's a decision of the Serbian Assembly appointing Jovan Cizmovic as coordinator of the work between the executive bodies and governments of the Serb Autonomous Regions and ARK. It is type-signed by Mr. Krajisnik, and dated the 21st of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remind us again, what is the difference between the Serb Autonomous Regions and the Municipal Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: The Serb Autonomous Regions had already been established and verified by the Bosnian Serb Assembly at this time. The municipalities fell under various autonomous regions. ARK, the Autonomous Region of Krajina, was one. There were also other autonomous regions. The regions were an intervening level between the municipalities and the republican level.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next, Your Honours, I'd like to move to tab number 36, which is master tab number 385. This is yet one more intercepted conversation, dated the 16th of January, 1992. I think it says the 15th on the tab and it says 16th on the document itself. And the portion that we want to play in the English begins on page 7, about halfway down, with Mr. Cizmovic speaking, saying, "Let me tell you this ..." We're ready, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Jovan CIZMOVIC: Let me tell you this: As far as I'm concerned, I'll help you with anything that's necessary. You know that. Radovan KARADZIC: Yes, sure thing. Jovan CIZMOVIC: I have talked to Bijeljina, how they have prepared for full cooperation. It's the same case with northern Bosnia. I've prepared a small, sort of, questionaire for all of them. Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh. Jovan CIZMOVIC: What have they managed to do? How far have they come? Radovan KARADZIC: Mhm. Jovan CIZMOVIC: To what extent are they prepared to implement the first level of the instructions? What are the problems? What do they need help with? I'm even prepared to form a sort of team with your help. A team that would possibly give them professional help with anything they find problematic. Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh. Jovan CIZMOVIC: With turning subjects of special importance into socially-owned companies and so on. Radovan KARADZIC: Yes, yes. Excellent. Jovan CIZMOVIC: Therefore, I'll try to do it ... to make it work."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand from the court reporter that at that speed, it's very difficult to keep up with the transcript. I don't know that we're yet following the process we talked about. I understood what you recited, and what I understood before, we played it through, one of the two interpreters listened to the B/C/S, then when it was through, the other one read from the English, the first one who had listened to the B/C/S advised him or her of whether or not what was on the English was what they had heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. From what I understood is that one of the interpreters would listen to the B/C/S original and would look at the same time on the English written translation to see whether the translation corresponded with the originally spoken words, and that at the same time, the other interpreter would start reading but in a -- at a pace which could be followed by the transcribers, the English translation, but would be a bit behind when finishing the English text compared to the original B/C/S spoken words.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And as I recall, we had the interpreter who was reading from the English transcript was also announcing changes of speakers by identifying the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't remember that detail, as a matter of fact, but at least if there would be any inconsistency between the English translation and the original spoken B/C/S words, which is not a full check of the translation but at least to see whether the translation covers the same text as originally spoken in B/C/S, that she would identify that -- that he or she would identify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Hannis's observation was 100 per cent correct. That's exactly how we remember it, that the interpreter was to identify changes of speakers, because otherwise it had become from time to time extremely confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that means that if the translation was read out, it would include the names of those speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that was -- I do distinctly remember that it was what we discussed and implemented at one point, and it was very helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore, I take it that the interpreters have followed this discussion, so reading out would include the names of those speaking. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, do you have a comment on that conversation?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Well, the conversation shows that Cizmovic is reporting to Karadzic. He has mentioned that he's talked to Bijeljina in northern Bosnia. Northern Bosnia was one of the Serb Autonomous Regions. And that he is helping them implement the first level of instructions. The word he uses for instructions is "uputstvo", although I would note that he doesn't say "level", he says "phase" in the original. So "uputstvo" is the word but not "stepan". However, if you connect that to the previous intercept, that Cizmovic was appointed to implement what was issued on the 20th of December, he is now reporting to Karadzic on the implementation in the municipalities and in the SAOs on the instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to go to the next binder, if we could hand you binder number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We'll go to presentation tab 37, Your Honours, in the second binder. This is master tab 386. This is the hard copy of the transcript of the sixth session of the Assembly of the Serbian People on the 26th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just come back to that last observation made by the witness. Ms. Hanson, you said -- you referred to the previous intercept, and you said, "he was appointed." I do understand that Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik are discussing the position of Mr. Cizmovic, and that the people for Krajina are dissatisfied with him. But who appointed him, exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the appointment shows it was the Assembly, the Serbian Assembly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was the assembly that appointed Mr. Cizmovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Coordinator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Coordinator. For what, exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It said, the work of the governments and executive boards of the SAOs and the ARK, the Serb Autonomous Regions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And there's no specific reference to Crisis Staffs or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you conclude from the discussion under tab 34, and this discussion, that his task included or was mainly about the implementation of the instructions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was part of his tasking, yes. As we'll see in the next reference, it's another reference of Cizmovic to the 19 December instructions. So it's a series of documents; one by one, hard to explain, but together I think they show ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In connection with that tab 37, as I mentioned, we will want to highlight a portion that, in the English, Your Honour, is on page number 14. If you can see in the lower right-hand corner, hopefully your copies of those pages have a page number, it's page number 4, and Mr. Cizmovic is speaking. The second paragraph up from the bottom that begins "To solve this problem ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, if you would please use your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if it's regarding the B/C/S, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am really unable to follow the course of all this. Would you please kindly tell me the number of the page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour, I can do that. The ERN number at the top right-hand corner is SA025260, and we've put the B/C/S up on the screen in the Sanction presentation. I don't know if Mr. Krajisnik can see that where he sits or not. And on that page, it is the second paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If everyone has found that, I'll ask Ms. Hanson to read it out for us.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: The B/C/S or the English?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can read the English.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Okay. "To solve this problem, I propose that we begin with an urgent operationalisation and a declaration on the establishment and promulgation of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Tasks set out in the instructions of 19 December 1991 should be carried out."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was -- these were remarks by Mr. Cizmovic in an assembly session chaired by Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any further discussion in that session about the instructions?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, can you now -- is that sort of the last reference where Mr. Cizmovic makes reference --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It's a series of documents on Cizmovic. Just to recap, we know that the 19 December instructions were distributed around about the 20th of December, sometime by the 23rd of December. We know that Cizmovic was appointed in order to implement something issued on the 20th of December. The implementation involved running from municipality to municipality, telling them, Do this, do this. That's from the intercept. He reported to Karadzic on the implementation of instructions in at least one municipality and one Serb region, and at the assembly he urged the implementation of the 19 December instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's move on from Mr. Cizmovic, and I want to ask you about whether or not your -- your review of the documents showed that the instructions were being implemented in some of the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to the formation of Crisis Staffs that we already showed, I saw many other references to the 19 December instructions that indicated they were received and implemented, and moreover, they were received as a legal basis for further action. I see many references to these instructions in the preamble to decisions of the Crisis Staff or of Serbian municipalities, referring to the instructions as a legal basis for their actions, which I think is indicative of the weight which they accorded this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with that, let's go through a few of those. Tab number 38, master tab number 50, a document dated 5 April 1992. And up on the screen, can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is an order of the commander of the Bosanska Krupa Crisis Staff. He is ordering the full mobilisation of the police stations. And the preamble says it's pursuant to the instructions for the organisation and activities of the Serb people of BiH in extraordinary circumstances. You will recall that activating the reserve police and taking over the police station was one of the steps in the 19 December instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab number 39, master tab number 52, dated the 15th of February, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is the decision on the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Donji Vakuf, and this decision, it says, it pursuant to Article 4 of the instructions for the organisation and activities of the organs of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in extraordinary circumstances of 19 December 1991. So a clear reference to the instructions, and cited along with the constitution and other decisions as a legal basis for their action, which is declaring the Serb municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next is tab number 40, master tab number 57.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is the decision on the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Tuzla, dated the 3rd of March, 1992. The wording is just the same as the previous document, pursuant to Article 4 of the 19 December instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab number 41, master tab number 58, from the 27th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Sorry. The decision on the formation of the Serb municipality of Zvornik. Same wording, same reference, pursuant to Article 4 of the 19 December instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also in that regard, tab number 42, which is master tab number 53, dated the 3rd of January, 1992, from Ilidza municipality.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. The proclamation of the Serb assembly of Ilidza municipality. Similarly, in the preamble it says, according to the instructions given by the BiH Serbian Democratic Party, Main Board, number 079, from 19 December 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the number 079 refers to?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: We haven't seen a 079 of the 19 December instructions, but that numbering is consistent with the style of numbering of the 19 -- those versions of the 19 December instructions we do have. So --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does that document, on the second page, indicate to whom copies of this decision were sent?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Yes. It says it was sent to the personal attention of the president of the Serbian Assembly of BiH, also to the president of the SDS and the SDS Main Board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks you. I'd like to go to tab number 43, which is master tab number 468. This is from the Bosnian Serb Assembly session in November of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, we want to direct your attention to a particular excerpt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask you one question. You say it was sent to the personal attention of the president of the Serbian Assembly of BiH. That appears on page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In English, it appears --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says just "attention," but in -- the B/C/S says "naruke," to the hand of. Perhaps -- I took that to mean personal attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first try to find it exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It's on page 2, at the bottom of the page 2 where it says "submitted to."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, could you look at the B/C/S copy.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: SA024140, and read item number 1 under the person sent to.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It says: [Interpretation] It is submitted to the Serbian Assembly of BiH for the attention of the president.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Personal attention was maybe my excessive translation. "Naruke" sounded like into the hand of but "attention" is apparently the most efficient. I wasn't trying to read more into it than was there in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to move to tab 43, master tab 468, the November 1994 Assembly session.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the number of the document. We haven't got it. Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you put off your microphone, that at least gives some relief to the interpreters, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab number 43, master tab number 468. This is the minutes of the Republika Srpska Assembly session from November of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the full session is in the master tab, in the exhibit. We just have an excerpt here that we want to show you. For Mr. Krajisnik, it's on the ERN page number 02153546, beginning seven lines up from the bottom. And the English, Your Honours, it's on page -- at the bottom, it should say page 347 of 411, beginning three lines up with the word "Please ..."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, could you read us that excerpt? And tell us who's speaking.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is Radovan Karadzic. There's been some discussion at this point in the assembly about forming more presidencies. Again, this is later, it's not the continuation of the War Presidencies of '92. "Please, remember how we used to work before the war. Everything was as clear as day in the municipalities where we were in the majority and in those where we were minority. Do you remember the instruction A and instruction B? We had Crisis Staffs, and it was clear that they were the authority. They could make mistakes, but they still were the authority. The people were not left without authority because there was a Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me move next to tab number 44, which has master tab number 49. This is, again, from an assembly session. This is the April 16th, 1995 session. And the excerpt that we want to bring to your attention now is, in the B/C/S, at page number 00846058, beginning ten lines from the top of the page, and in the English, it's the page number at the bottom listed as 323 of 389, and it begins approximately two-thirds of the way down with the sentence that begins "At the moment the war began ..." Can you tell us who's speaking there?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is, again, Radovan Karadzic talking about the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there are, I believe, two segments that you've highlighted. When you've reached the end of the first one, can you tell us where you're skipping to to begin the second?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: The second highlighting is actually -- I want to refer to that passage at another point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: I didn't get into the technology of different copies and highlighting, so I'm just doing the first highlighting part right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: "At the moment the war began, in the municipalities where they were in the majority, we had municipal power, held it firmly, controlled everything. In the municipalities where we were in the minority, we set up secret government, municipal boards, municipal assemblies, presidents of executive boards. You will remember the A and B variants. In the B variant, where we were in the minority, 20 per cent/15 per cent, we had set up a government and a brigade, a unit, no matter what size, but there was a detachment with a commander."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll move next to -- pardon me. Let me move next to tab 45.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're going on to a different topic now. I want to talk about the portion of Ms. Hanson's report that refers to contacts between Crisis Staffs and the leadership prior to the actual takeovers in the assemblies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, tab number 45 is master tab number 69, a document dated the 1st of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. This is --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about that one?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is a report from the Crisis Staff of Bijeljina, addressed to the SDS Main Board in Sarajevo, reporting on the situation in Bijeljina on the 1st of April. I found it significant that the Crisis Staff in this case is reporting to the SDS Main Board. It's indicative of the fact that the Crisis Staff saw themselves as much to be SDS organs as, by this time in April, government organs. There are -- in this time period, from the issuance of the 19 December instructions until April, the process at both the republican level and reflected also at the municipal level was the transformation of the SDS organs into a Bosnian state organs. That's the discussion we saw in the assembly of how we do we form our state and our state organs. And this is the process. It's ongoing. And I wanted to indicate that during this time period, the contacts between the municipal level and the republican level continued. So in this case, this is a report to the Main Board; some via the assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Related to that there's another document at tab number 46, which is master tab number 70, dated 28 February 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry to interrupt you. I'd like to go back to tab 45. Ms. Hanson, what do you mean in paragraph 2? Can you have an explanation for us regarding paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The movement of citizens?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: Between 2000 and 0600.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume that to be a curfew, to mean a curfew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, are you aware of approximately when there were combat activities in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. We have another report that says that the 31st of March to the 1st of April was the takeover of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, let me particular you to tab 46, master tab number 70, a document dated 28 February 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is the session of the municipal board of the SDS Novo Sarajevo. This municipal board had some internal conflict on some discussion of the work of the president. And at the end of this document, on page 2 of the translation in the original, it says that -- the last line, in fact, says: "The discussion of whether they can --" it is their job to discuss the work of the Crisis Staff. And a member says: "The Bosnian Serb assembly formed the Crisis Staff, and it," meaning the assembly, "should discuss the work of the Crisis Staff." So it's -- I found it indicative at the municipal level, they're saying the Crisis Staff should be reporting to the assembly; the assembly should be checking -- discussing the work of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, apart from some of the Crisis Staff documents, did you see other reflections, for example, in assembly sessions, that there was communication between the center and the Crisis Staffs prior to the actual beginnings of takeovers?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. You will recall that, according to the 19 December instructions, assembly deputies were members of their respective municipal Crisis Staffs. And we see from the assembly sessions, there was much discussion of how to realise the creation of the Serbian state on the ground, at the municipal level, and we see from the assembly discussions the importance of the assembly deputies in that process. The assembly deputies were the link from the republican level to the municipal, so that's -- the next series of documents referred to those communications in the assembly and as referred to in the assembly between the republican and municipal level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me take you, then, to tab 47 in the presentation binder, which is master tab 387, from the 25 February 1992 eighth assembly session. The B/C/S excerpt, for Mr. Krajisnik, is at page SA025489, and it's the paragraph -- the three-line paragraph in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the English, it's the page numbered at the bottom 44. Again, the paragraph appears to be in the middle of the page and begins "I have good contact ..."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who's speaking there?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Karadzic is, again, speaking. The discussion here, in general, is the Autonomous Region of the Krajina. In addition to that highlighted passage, I just summarised what else he says. At the top of that page, in the English translation, he says that: "Every municipality is following our political line." The only thing he cannot forgive the -- a small number of people in Banja Luka, the problems he's having with the ARK leadership, is they say what they're doing is their creation, "it's all our line," he says. "We are the ones who conceived it all." Then the highlighted section: "I have good contact with all municipalities, and there is not a single municipality in Krajina which does not support what the SDS has accomplished so far." Then skipping one paragraph, at the beginning of the last paragraph, in the English translation, it says: "I have been to Banja Luka 27 times." I think it's important -- this speech is important, I think, for showing how much Karadzic is in contact with the municipalities, feels that all the municipalities are following the SDS policies, and support what the SDS is doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to move to tab number 48 in the presentation binder, master tab number 388, from the 18th March 1992 assembly session. In the B/C/S, the excerpt we want to talk about is at the top of page SA025765.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, in the English version, I believe we're starting at the bottom of page numbered 38 of 49, the second paragraph up from the bottom of the page, which begins "So our job here ..."

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is Miroslav Jezestica, a member of the Crisis Staff of Bosanska Krupa and deputy in the assembly, talking about what has been done to establish Serbian power in Krupa. "So our job here is to decide whether we have the organisational potential to establish our police, our territorial defence, to have our commander, establish the money transfer system, and take possession of our territories, as well as when to do these things. Bosanska Krupa is textbook example. It's been six months now since the current MUP inspections or other services have not been to our Serbian territories around Mount Grmac in this area of Serbian municipalities. They cannot. We do not let them. They do not dare to. We have de facto occupied our own territories. But here we must reach an agreement that all Serbs in all municipalities, both the newly formed and the existing ones, take over the power, because we have not taken over. Mr. President, I think you have to give us an order, that after the next session of the assembly, you should order this, that we arrange it for the areas where it has not been done and implement this; that the Serbs should occupy their territories so that no other forces could enter them."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reference to "Mr. President ..."

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: I assume to be president of the assembly, because he is saying -- he's talking at the assembly. The convention in the assembly, generally, as I understood it, is that the speakers would address the speaker of the assembly as President, Mr. President of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do the minutes of that assembly session reflect who was the president presiding on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Mr. Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tab number 49, master tab number 389, there's another excerpt from the assembly session of 24 March 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me see if I can find the appropriate page reference. This is Mr. Jezestica speaking in the B/C/S at page number SA025816.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, the English --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I have the wrong -- yes, 5815. And in the English, it's on page 20, beginning -- the English begins in the fourth paragraph down from the top. Who's speaking there?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It's Miroslav Jezestica, again -- once again, informing the assembly of what has been accomplished at the municipal level and seeking further directions from the assembly for actions at the municipal level. "We, who have no authority, we have our chief, our commander, our police. We have the territory we occupied and no one is trying to cross over into it." So he's telling the assembly how they have established power in his municipality. And then he speaks again, the next speech by Vjestica. It's in the same page of the translation, but the next page in the B/C/S. He says: "Appoint the ministers and agree on the assumption of power in our Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. We can then go home with our piece of homework, to assume power in our Serbian republic of BH."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any other comment on that before we go to the next tab?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Just, once again, the inter-play between the municipal and the -- assembly level. Give us our instructions and we'll carry them out at the municipal level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Presentation tab 50, master tab 389, another assembly session excerpt from the 24th of March, 1992. And in the B/C/S, I think the page number is SA025810.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two paragraphs up from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In the English, Your Honours, we are on page 17, about five paragraphs up from the bottom, which begins "The deputies are members ..."

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It's Karadzic speaking, talking once again about what do we do now as the -- at this moment, he says: "The deputies are members of the supreme organ of authority, the assembly. Now they must literally stay with the presidents of municipalities. A municipality president is basically the one who should be obeyed. This is the way it must be." And in the next paragraph, he says at the end of the paragraph: "The president of the municipality is the one who carries out our plans." So I think it shows, once again, the relationship between the assembly and the municipal level. The deputy goes from the assembly to the municipality, works with the municipal president who is the one who, at the municipal level, has the power to carry out the plans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presentation tab 51, master tab number 389, also from the 24th of March, 1992, assembly session. Again, Mr. Karadzic speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The B/C/S reference is at page number SA025819, about four lines down in the second paragraph. In the English, Your Honours, page number 22, the big paragraph in the middle of the page, about four lines down, beginning with the phrase "And this will be very soon ..."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It's, once again, Karadzic telling the deputies that soon they will be taking power. "This will be very soon. We can form whatever we want. There are reasons why this could happen in two or three days. Such are the forecasts, but I cannot tell you the reasons now. At that moment, all the Serbian municipalities, both the old ones and the newly established ones would literally assume control of the entire territory of the municipality concerned. The Zvornik municipality takes control over everything that constitutes the Serbian municipality of Zvornik. Then, at a given moment, in the next three or four days, there will be a single method used, and you will be able to apply it in the municipalities you represent, including both things that must be done as well as how to do them; how to separate the police force, take the resources that belong to the Serbian people, and take command. The police must be under the control of the civilian authority. They must obey it. There is no discussion about it. That's the way it must be. I think we shall hear it today in the form of instructions at the deputy's club." So Karadzic is, once again, showing that instructions will come from the republic level to the municipalities, and the municipal -- the assembly deputies will get these instructions, go to the municipalities, and help the formation -- help take power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Near the end of the paragraph, the remark about separating the police force and taking resources that belong to the Serbian people, does that reflect anything in the variant A document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, these were both itemised in the variant A as some of the steps. Taking over resources, forming a Serbian police, are all part of the instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next I'd like to move to presentation tab 52 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Pardon me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask one additional question. The words spoken, "there will be a single method used and you'll be able to apply it in the municipalities," how do you understand this part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That there would be one set of instructions. All the municipalities will follow certain steps to take over power. That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In regard to that last question, can you relate that to anything about the variant A and B instructions?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Well, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that's the answer to the question, really, isn't it? If the question is put in that form, it might not as well be answered, because Mr. Hannis has given the question and the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure that the question calls for a yes or no. If the answer is yes, then I'll ask what it is that she can relate it to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, leading questions generally do ask for a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Leading questions suggest the answer you're seeking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are two types of leading questions; one is in which the answer is already suggested, and the other type, I have to think about that, which starts from a factual point of view which has not been established yet. I think these are the two types of leading questions we have. Let me just reread it. I think the witness could answer to the following question: When you said there would be one set of instructions, "all the municipalities will follow certain steps to take over power," would that mean that it would be the same for variant A and variant B municipalities, because you are talking about one set, where the instructions seem to give different sets of instructions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there's not that much difference between the A and B variants in step 2 as to what they should be doing. The difference, mostly, is in where those measures are to be undertaken, because it specifies that in variant B, it's in those areas that are Serb-inhabited as opposed to throughout the whole municipality. But the steps themselves are quite similar between variant A and variant B at level 2. The things -- what they're supposed to do is quite similar. The reason I did not refer -- I -- the -- because Karadzic says at the end of the speech that "we will get instructions today at the deputy's club," he's not necessarily speaking of the 19 December instructions, because he's saying, You will get them. He's not saying, You have received this already, but "instructions will come today at the deputy's club." That's why I think he's saying there will be one set of instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thanks very much. Please proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, I'll move to tab number 52, which is master tab number 72, an excerpt from the fourteenth session of the assembly, 27 March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I believe the B/C/S excerpt begins on page number SA025873. And the English is at page number 20, at the bottom, near the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, is this correct, the paragraph that begins "When you return ..."

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. "When you return to your municipalities, specially the newly formed municipalities, I ask you to do what you're required and entitled to do under the law. The moment you arrive in your municipalities, you must urgently establish Crisis Staffs. You must try to organise the people so they can defend themselves. Find a number of reserve officers for those staffs and have them register everyone who owns weapons as well as units. They should organise territorial defence, and if the JNA is there, they must be placed under its command." Then skipping the rest of that paragraph and the next paragraph, in the paragraph beginning "a war in Bosnia," he says: "I urge you to immediately organise the people within Territorial Defence units headed by reserve officers. Form squads, platoons, and Crisis Staffs, and engage retired officers. This must be done throughout our areas. The presidents of municipalities and executive boards will hold the highest ranks in the Crisis Staffs in addition to reserve officers. We must study the situation regarding the saving of lives, property, and territory. We have no other plans." These are all, again, consistent with the 19 December instructions; organising the TO; where possible, subordinate the police to the JNA commands; that the presidents of the municipalities and executive boards will hold the highest ranks in the Crisis Staff; instructions on saving lives, property, and territory. Those are all elements of the 19 December instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any additional part of that excerpt that you wanted to talk about, like you've highlighted five paragraphs down --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's another page on the board. Yes, there was more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For Mr. Krajisnik, I think that would be another five paragraphs down from where you left off.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: I'm just trying to see -- yes, it's on the next page in the English, page 21, fifth paragraph down. "I urge you to undertake with the full authorisation of the assembly the task of introducing discipline and organising Crisis Staffs headed by reserve and retired officers to organise the people for defensive purposes." I find it significant he says, "the full authorisation of the assembly." It's not clear here whether he means this assembly or the municipal assembly, but because we have heard him in the assembly saying "form Crisis Staffs," I take it to mean he's telling the deputies, You have our authorisation here in the assembly to go form Crisis Staffs. Then the next speaker, Savo Knezevic, this is all on page 21 and on page SA025874, says: "What if the municipality president doesn't want to do what we're telling him? Rejects our proposals?" And Karadzic says: "If they don't want to act, they should be warned." First of all, Knezevic reveals an expectation -- an expectation of reporting, should we let you know what's going on in the municipality if the president doesn't want to carry out our plans, and Karadzic is repeating what he said before, that the presidents of the municipalities have the executive power at the municipal level to actually carry out our plans. The deputies take the plans there, and it's the municipality president who carries them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, I'd like to do one more before the break. Tab number 53 in the presentation binder, which is master tab 73, a document dated 4 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that is, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is a public announcement of the National Security Council, signed and stamped by Karadzic as president of the National Security Council. In the last paragraph, he says -- it's reacting to an announcement of the Bosnian presidency, that is, the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia, not the Bosnian-Serb presidency. And he says that should they respond to the call for mobilisation, "the Serb council for national defence instructs that Crisis Staffs be activated in such areas, and the readiness of the Territorial Defence be raised, as well as the Serb people's civilian defence and Serb police." I find it significant -- first of all, it's a public reference to Crisis Staffs, and it is Karadzic speaking as president of the National Security Council, not president of the SDS. And this marks, I would say, the full public activation of Crisis Staffs, moving from secret party organs to public government organs. And similarly, the National Security Council now speaking as an organ of the Bosnian Serb state, so it's Karadzic, as president of the National Security Council, not the SDS, saying Crisis Staffs should be activated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this may be a few minutes early, but I'm about to go into a new area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And since this second break is usually a bit shorter and taken a bit earlier, we will adjourn until a quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we proceed, the Chamber was informed that there were some problems that is available now to Mr. Krajisnik. At the same time, it seems that Mr. Krajisnik has not been informed that, due to the fact that the agreement was not yet signed by counsel, that, for the time being, Mr. Krajisnik, you are only allowed to use the laptop in this courtroom, not to take anything from that laptop to the United Nations Detention Unit, so either, I think, give it to counsel on a CD or keep it on the laptop. At least that's the present situation. I think that the counsel could, at an appropriate time, further inform you about the matters. Let me just --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, I can, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just a moment. We're not going to spend time on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the agreement was signed, but that amendments were still to be signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not a matter, in my view, that should be dealt with in court at this moment, unless it has a direct bearing on the proceedings at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fact, Your Honour has dealt with what was going to be a comment of mine about the sense of what Your Honour had just said. But thank you, that is dealt with, because it's not that it's simply haven't been gotten round to. I want to tell so that Mr. Krajisnik knowings right now, because it's a convenient way of informing him as it happens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, court time on these kind of matters, of course, and any issues. I'll ask otherwise that Mr. Krajisnik will be directly informed, or you seek any assistance of an interpreter, but at this moment we prefer to continue --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I could have informed him in less time than the comments Your Honour has just made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like next to go to presentation tab 54, master tab 443, assembly session 24 March 1992, and the excerpt that we want to talk about is at page 8 of the English. This is Mr. Vjestica speaking again. And in the B/C/S, it is on page SA025838, on the bottom of the page where Mr. Vjestica is shown. Ms. Hanson, can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, as you said, it's Vjestica's speech, once again, the discussion on forming a Bosnian state. He summarises the debate so far as saying that the assembly should adopt a conclusion, instructing the prime minister of the Serbian republic and the ministers to prepare an operational plan for assuming power so the assembly can decide when to take power. The last sentence: "This should be simultaneously affected in all municipalities where we already have a Serbian authority, and in those municipalities where we have only recently established Serbian municipalities." Then, to continue on the next page of the translation and the original, Mr. Krajisnik then sums up the debate as saying: "So the conclusion is that we give the -- the government should draw up a plan for us." And then Branko Dzeric, the prime minister, then says -- responds to this, saying: "The government will have the duty to draw up an operational plan and to submit it for adoption." His last sentence: "Please do not take things in your own hands. You will receive your instructions and you will proceed as instructed." This is indicative of this time period where the assembly is much concerned with creating the state and empowering the organs that they have set up, including the government. And the government is clearly assuming responsibility for the steps to be taken at the municipal level. The prime minister is saying, Don't take things into your own hands, wait for the government's instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And subsequent to that date, were there some instructions from the government to Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The 26th of April, Dzeric, as prime minister or president of the government --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, let me interrupt and say for the record, Your Honour, we'll go to presentation tab 55, master tab number 76.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This document is the instructions issued by Dzeric as prime minister on the 26th of April, 1992. The document is called "Excerpt from the Instructions for the Operation of Crisis Staffs of the Serbian People and Municipalities."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there similarities between this document and the earlier variant A and variant B document we've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, there are similarities. Under item 2, discussing the makeup and the assignments of the Crisis Staff, you'll see it's quite similar to the 19 December instructions, naming president, deputy president, territorial staff commander, president of the executive board, head of the MUP; and then the various taskings for various members, economy, humanitarian and health, information, propaganda, supplies and diet or food, those are all mentioned as various tasks of the 19 December instructions, various steps to be taken. Refugees, war crimes, not specifically, but liaison and coordination are also taskings given in the 19 December instructions. So it's very similar to the 19 December instructions in that sense. It's also significant, the first item, that the Crisis Staff will take over all prerogatives and functions of the municipal assemblies. They are, essentially, becoming the municipal government. We'll see that consistently throughout, both the normative documents and what the Crisis Staffs say about themselves. Item 3, to coordinate functions, to protect territory and safety, setting up authority, organising all other streams of life and work, they are the municipal authorities, they are to coordinate all the various forces and resources in the municipality. Item 6 is significant, because it says that the Crisis Staffs' actions shall be based on constitutional and legal provisions and on the decisions of the assembly, the presidency, and the government. So Crisis Staffs are to act according to the decisions of the republican organs, the municipality -- the assembly, and the presidency and the government. Item 11 shows the reporting duty of Crisis Staffs; to notify and consult the competent authorities of the Serbian BiH, that is, commissioners. This is the first mention we have of commissioners. We'll see them again in later documents. The commissioners, as we will see, were personal links between the state leadership and the municipal level. Item 14 also mandates reporting to the regional and state organs of the BiH. I guess not all the pages got in Sanction. So it shows -- it shows Crisis Staffs as the municipal authorities, as coordinating bodies for all the different forces in the municipality, and indicates the breadth of their authority and their role within the Serbian state; that they are to act according to the decisions of the republic organs and report back to the state organs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you next included in your presentation some examples that indicate those instructions were actually disseminated and received within the municipalities?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. The next tab.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me cite that number: Presentation tab 56, master tab number 390.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is a decision of the municipal assembly of Bosanska Gradiska to confirm the regulations adopted by the War Presidency. As we see, that was one of the stipulations of the instructions for the work of Crisis Staffs that when municipal assemblies can meet, they should verify those decisions taken by the Crisis Staff. In the preamble, on the first page of the translation, the preamble says: "In conjunction with item 7 of the instructions for the work of Serbian Crisis Staffs and municipalities of 26 April 1992," so that is in -- evidence that those instructions were received, implemented, and granted legal authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next, let me take you to tab 57, master tab number 391. Tell us about that one.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: The decision on the formation of the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Bosanska Dubica is similarly taken pursuant to the instructions for the work of Crisis Staffs of the Serbian people and municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab number 58, master tab number 78.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pardon me. I would just like to know, to what does the Official Gazette correspond? If the witness can inform us on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correspond in what sense? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask you a question in that regard? Are you referring to the last tab that the Official Gazette of Bosanska Dubica municipality? Because there are more than one Official Gazettes that we'll talk about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good. So this is what I wanted to know. So this is the Official Gazette of the republic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of the municipality, yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The municipality had its own in addition to the republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was a republic -- Republika Srpska Official Gazette as well?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were decisions of local Crisis Staffs or municipal Crisis Staffs published in the state Official Gazette or the republic Official Gazette --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: No, they were published in the municipal gazette. Municipal decisions in the municipal gazette, and republic decisions in the republic gazette. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next, tab number 58 in the presentation binder, which is master tab number 78.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. This is the decision of the Serbian municipality of Bihac, dated the 21st of May, 1992, on appointment of members of the Crisis Staff. In its preamble, once again, it cites: "The instruction of the Serbian government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the excerpt from the instructions for the work of Crisis Staffs of the Serbian people and municipalities." Not only does it give that direct citation, but other articles are -- clearly reflect Dzeric's instructions. For example, number 2, the makeup corresponds to the taskings. And, in fact, on Article 9, they explicitly say that -- this is on the second page of the translation: "Crisis Staff members shall work and perform their duties in accordance with the instructions for the work of Crisis Staffs in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." So clear indication that the instructions were disseminated, implemented, and granted authority in the eyes of those who received it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll go to tab number 59 in the presentation binder, which is master tab number 100. Can you tell us about this one from the assembly of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: It's similar to the Bihac decision, but it's even more extensive. It's a decision on the organisation and work of the Crisis Staff of Prijedor municipality, and it similarly paraphrases or echoes Dzeric's instructions. Article 2 of the Prijedor instruction is -- I believe it's almost identical to Article 3 of Dzeric's instructions. Article 4, the makeup of the Prijedor municipality, is similarly consistent with Dzeric's instructions. Other articles are very close paraphrasings of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to these examples in some of the municipal staff Crisis Staff documents, did you see other reflections that indicated the instructions had been received and followed?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. We have an explicit statement to that effect in the assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me refer you to the next tab. Presentation number 60, master tab number 392. And for locating the excerpt in the B/C/S, it's at page number 02149523, I believe the second line; and in the English, Your Honours, it's on the page numbered 29 of 104, about eight lines up from the bottom, beginning "In one period we worked ..."

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. This is Milanovic, a deputy from Banja Luka. He says: "In one period we worked according to the government instructions and formed Crisis Staffs." So he's saying they got those instructions and formed Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tab number 61 in the presentation binder, which is master tab number 68, can you tell us about that document, who it's from and --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, this is an interesting document. I will refer to it later as well. It is from the secretary of the executive committee of the SDS, Trivko Komad, it says illegible, but under the circumstances we know it's Trivko, dated the 31st of May, 1992. It's addressed to the presidents of governments of three Serb Autonomous Regions. And it's reminding them that Crisis Staffs' structure and method of work and functioning were established by the instructions of the government of the Serbian Republic of BiH of 26 April 1992. So it's further evidence that these instructions were seen as the normative document at that time for Crisis Staffs. As we note, this letter will then go on to say they've been abolished to later decisions. We'll be looking at those decisions in a second. But the first reference to this letter shows that the instructions were -- had formed -- were the guidelines for the Crisis Staffs at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything else you want to talk about that document now, or is that for later?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: I think for later we'll -- well, just that the sentence continues that there's a decision on the establishment of War Presidencies of 31 May 1992. We'll be getting to that in a moment, so I'll keep my comments for then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That takes me to the next topic I want to talk about. In your report, you have a section --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one additional question in relation to it. It gives a number in handwriting at the top. Has that a specific meaning, just as -- well ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe this document was received from Rajko Dukic. He submitted a number of documents to the Tribunal. It may be that this was number 22 of the documents he gave. I don't know otherwise. Certainly, I would not assign any other significance to that number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not like limited distribution of copies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to go to a new section in your report. You talk about War Presidencies and War Commissions. Before we make that transfer, can you explain what the difference was between Crisis Staffs and War Presidencies and War Commissions?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: In my report, I explain that I take them to be much the same body. The -- as the Bosnian Serb state is being created, and the legal foundations are being written and the organs being actually empowered, there is a transition from Crisis Staffs to War Presidencies and War Commissions, but they are clearly various versions of essentially the same body. They are the municipality authorities that take over from municipal assemblies with all of the functions and prerogatives of a municipal asssembly. For that reason, I'll consider them as essentially the same body. Moreover, as we will see, there is considerable inconsistency in the way the terminology is applied. The people on the ground themselves used the terminology inter-changeably in a way that suggests they did not see or they weren't careful about the terminology because there wasn't an essential difference among those bodies. We'll see that the decisions on establishing War Presidencies and War Commissions come from the presidency of the BiH -- of the Serbian republic, excuse me. And it's an attempt -- it's part of the process, I would say, of normalising, legalising the situation. So I think it will become clear as we look at the steps to get there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was there some sort of government decision to abolish the Crisis Staffs and create these newer versions of local governing bodies?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, we see that in the next document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: For the record, this is presentation tab 62, master tab number 107.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about that, please.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: These are the minutes of the meeting of the government of the Serb republic, from the 23rd of May, 1992. If you go to article -- item 4, the government concludes that Crisis Staffs should be abolished. "Conditions for the functioning of regular organs should be created as soon as possible. Municipalities should be given all help in doing so." The government holds that War Presidencies should be established in municipalities. "The War Presidencies would govern for a certain period of time until all the preparations for creating the conditions for forming and work of regular governing organs have been carried out." So you can see that it's a -- they are in the transition, the transition to regular organs of government. How do we get there? Well, we'll start with War Presidencies to take over from Crisis Staffs, and when all the regular municipal organs can function, then we'll get back to the municipal assembly and the regular organs. So the transition here is from the original Crisis Staffs, as we know, created by the SDS, then form -- functioning as the municipal government, now to regularise the situation and get towards a -- towards a regular functioning municipal government, with all the organs empowered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was on the 23rd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following day, I want to direct you to a document which is presentation tab 63, master tab number 108. The next day, what is this document, who did it come from, and what is it about?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This document is signed by Biljana Plavsic for the presidency of the Serb Republic of BiH, dated the 24th of May, 1992, and it is instructions for the organisation and work of presidencicies and municipalities in conditions of the imminent threat of war and a state of war, directing municipalities to form presidencies. As I mentioned in my report, I don't know if I need to explain again, municipal assemblies had -- there was a president of the municipal assembly, but there was the concept of a collective body, a presidency, to replace them when they -- when assemblies could not meet in full. So it would not be a single president but a body of the leadership meeting to replace it. So this is -- that was in the original legislation of the Socialist Republic of Yugoslavia -- of Bosnia. Just to note quickly what Plavsic foresees as the purpose of these presidencies. To coordinate and create all conditions for the functioning of legal organs; accord and synchronise activities for defence; and enable the work of municipal organs and units. So there are -- the emphasis, again, on coordination and on enabling defence is an important one. Again, these instructions indicate a commissioner to -- the role of the commissioner, it says in the last -- second to last paragraph: "The commissioner is authorised to undertake all measures regarding the organisation and work of municipal presidencies, to ensure constant coordination and implementation of the policies," it says "of measures," but I believe it might be "measures, determined and issued by the public state organs and the Main Staff of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina," and "the commissioner appoints the presidency." So this shows a close tie from the republican level to the municipal. The commissioner is the link. He appoints the presidencies, and he is to coordinate what they do with republican organs, and also the Main Staff. So there's clearly a military role intended if part of the job of the municipal presidencies is to carry out the measures and policies of the Main Staff or General Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to this time with the Crisis Staff, was there any equivalent position, such as a commissioner, that was a link between the municipal Crisis Staffs and the republic organs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Well, we saw in Dzeric's instructions from the 26th of April, there was mention of a commissioner. We also -- that is the first use I have seen of the term "commissioner" in this context, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that was on the 24th of May. Let me take you to the 31st of May. The next document, presentation tab 64, master tab number 110. This appears to be another sequence in the evolution of these local governing bodies. Can you tell us about that one?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. This is the decision of the presidency of the Serb republic, signed by Karadzic as president of the presidency, dated the 31st of May, on the formation of War Presidencies in municipalities. Article 3 on the duties and authorities of a War Presidency are very similar to what we've seen in Plavsic's instructions: organise, coordinate, and adjust activities for the defence of the Serbian people and for the establishment of the law for municipal authorities; perform all the duties of the assembly and the executive body until those authorities are able to convene and work; create and ensure conditions for the work of military bodies and units. Once again, we'll see there will be a commissioner, and the phrasing is very similar on -- he is to ensure coordination and implementation of the policies and measures of the state organs and the Main Staff. So it's very similar to the previous instructions, but an emphasis, again, on the transition, "until the regular authorities can carry out work, we have these War Presidencies." Article 5, this is clearly meant to replace Crisis Staffs. "The day War Presidencies are established, Crisis Staffs will cease to operate."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this decision was published in the republic Official Gazette --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: Official Gazette, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me take you to the next document, presentation tab number 65, master tab number 111. Can you tell us briefly what that is?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON
utterances.text: This is an amendment to the constitution now allowing for a municipal presidency. That VRS constitution, until that point, had not had an allowance for municipal presidencies.
